version.description: The version being agreed to — the one the person was shown.

chapterIds.description: Narrow what they may change to these chapters. Omitted, the whole work.

name.description: What to call them, since an address is a poor way to recognise a friend.

chapterId.description: Required for a chapter-scoped question, ignored otherwise.

actorId.description: Who did it. Kept after their account is gone.

AuthorCard.description: Author cards attached to comments so the clients need no second round trip.

BlockChangeKind.description: One paragraph's fate between two versions.

beforeIndex.description: Index of this paragraph in the earlier version, when it was in it.

changes.description: Word-level detail, for a modified paragraph.

counts.description: Totals, for the author only — see the note on `list_reactions`.

oneOf.description: What the viewer themselves marked, if anything.

quote.description:
The opening of the paragraph, so the author's list reads as prose
rather than as coordinates. Empty if the block has since gone.

userId.description:
Who to shut out. An id rather than an address: this is somebody who has
already turned up.

authorId.description: Only this author's proposals, when set.

stale.description:
Proposals whose text has moved on too far to place automatically. They
stay pending: refusing is safer than guessing where they meant.

commentIds.description: Named ids win outright; without them the filters below choose.

chapterIds.description:
The chapters they may change, when they were handed only some. Absent
means the whole work.

email.description:
The address it went to. Shown to owners only: the people on a book do
not need each other's addresses to work on it.

oneOf.description: Who they are, once they have an account and have opened the work.

authorScore.description:
How useful this reviewer's notes have proved elsewhere — votes plus the
notes authors marked resolved. Shown beside the name so a reader with a
record of being right is legible as one.

replies.description:
Threads nest arbitrarily deep, which makes this type self-referential.
Schema generation has to be told to stop, or it recurses until the stack
gives out.

payload.description:
The replacement text for `insert` and `replace`, or the mark name for
`format`. Ignored for `delete`.

oneOf.description: Present for highlight-to-comment; absent for a general note.

maxReviewers.description: How many people may comment. Omitted, there is no cap.

scopeRefId.description: Chapter or scene id when `scope` is narrower than the whole work.

spoilerSafe.description:
Withhold notes on scenes a reader has not reached. Omitted, it follows
the work: on for a serial, off for anything else.

scope.description: `work` asks it once; `chapter` asks it of every chapter on offer.

oneOf.description:
`work` (the default), `chapter` or `scene`. A smaller snapshot is for
checkpointing one chapter before rewriting it, without implying
anything about the rest of the book.

scopeRefId.description: The chapter or scene being frozen, when narrower than the whole work.

templateId.description: Omit for a single empty chapter and scene.

code.description: From the authenticator, when two-factor sign-in is on.

deleteSharedWorks.description:
Required when a work being deleted has co-authors on it, after they
have been told which.

from.description: What each side is called — a version's label, or "Working draft".

oneOf.description: The version behind each side, absent when it is the working copy.

code.description: From the authenticator, or a recovery code.

DocNode.description:
The document shape, declared for the generated schema.

The server stores and forwards scene bodies as opaque `serde_json::Value` —
the editor owns the schema, and the server has no reason to validate beyond
`validate()` above. But "opaque" would generate as `unknown` in the clients,
which is exactly the kind of untyped hole this contract exists to close, so
the fields carrying a document declare this type instead.

sceneIds.description: Scenes this entry appears in, in reading order.

details.description: Present when the client is expected to act on it — see a scene save conflict.

requestId.description: The request's id, as in its `x-request-id` header and its log lines.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
The shape every failure comes back as. Declared for the generated schema so
clients can type their error handling instead of guessing.

circleId.description: Invite everyone in one of the author's circles, by id.

emails.description: Addresses to invite. Duplicates and ones already invited are ignored.

accepted.description: Whether that reader has opened it yet.

ticket.description: Single use, good for thirty seconds: `GET /api/live?ticket=…`.

code.description:
The six digits from an authenticator, or a recovery code, for an
account with two-factor sign-in on. Asked for with a
`two_factor_required` refusal when it is missing.

baseHash.description: Both scenes' hashes, so a merge cannot silently swallow someone's edit.

with.description: The scene to absorb. It must sit in the same chapter.

changes.description: Word-level detail for an edited paragraph.

now.description: What that paragraph says now, when it still says anything.

NoteStatus.description: What became of the text a note was attached to.

oneOf.description:
The caller's standing on the work, so a client can offer only what the
server will accept. Sent on every outline; optional so an outline a
client cached before collaboration existed still decodes.

publications.description:
What this author has on offer that the viewer could open — the same
rule the feed applies, so a profile never lists a locked door.

reviews.description: Other people's work this person has given notes on, newest first.

viewerFollows.description: Whether the person asking follows this author. Always false signed out.

sceneId.description: The scene the reader is looking at.

maxReviewers.description:
How many people may comment. Beta readers are scarce, and twenty
overlapping opinions are worse than five considered ones.

spoilerSafe.description:
Withhold notes on scenes a reader has not reached yet. Defaulted on for
a serial, where not knowing yet is the whole point of reading one.

authorReviewsGiven.description:
Other people's publications this author has left notes on — what lifts
their work in the needs-readers queue.

excerpt.description:
First lines of the published slice, for the feed. Filled in after the
database round trip because it comes off disk — always sent, even when
empty, so clients do not have to treat it as optional.

readerCount.description: Distinct people who have opened it or left a note, the author excepted.

snippet.description:
Words around what a search matched, when this card came from one;
matched words sit between U+0002 and U+0003.

baseHash.description:
The `contentHash` the client believes it is editing on top of. When it
no longer matches, someone else — another tab, another device, a queued
offline save — has written in the meantime, and this save is refused
rather than silently overwriting their work.

Omitted only when there is nothing to protect: a scene the client has
not read yet. To resolve a conflict deliberately, re-send with the hash
the 409 reported, which says "I have seen their version and still mean
this".

createRevision.description: Autosaves pass `false`; explicit saves and idle-flushes pass `true`.

localDay.description:
The writer's local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, so this save counts toward the
right day. Omitted, it is not recorded against any day at all: skipping
a tally is better than crediting the wrong one.

blockIndex.description: Index of the paragraph in the snapshot scene.

kind.description: Sending the kind already there clears it, the way a repeated vote does.

percent.description: Furthest point reached, as a percentage of the published scenes.

furthestIndex.description:
The furthest they ever reached, which is the interesting one: a reader
who gave up in chapter three and later skimmed the ending has still
stopped in chapter three.

codes.description: Shown once. Each gets someone in once if the authenticator is lost.

acceptTerms.description: Agreement to the terms in force (`GET /api/terms`). Required.

ids.description: Complete ordered list of ids; anything missing keeps its current slot.

commentBody.description: What was said, so the author can judge without going to find it.

oneOf.description: The scene as it stands after applying it, when one was applied.

outline.description: The work's outline, as it now stands.

safetyVersion.description: The snapshot taken of the working copy before it was replaced.

scenesRemoved.description:
Scenes that existed only in the working copy and were removed. They are
in `safetyVersion`, which is the point of taking it.

ReviewHistoryItem.description: One publication someone reviewed, as their profile shows it.

resolved.description: Notes the author marked resolved — that they acted on it.

commentId.description:
The note it came from, or `None` for one the author typed themselves —
or one whose comment has since been deleted. The task is the author's
either way.

blocks.description:
Paragraph-aligned diff against the scene as it stands now — what
restoring this revision would change.

storyDate.description: Free text: fiction rarely runs on the Gregorian calendar.

targetWords.description: A target for this scene, for writers who plan at that level.

blocks.description: Paragraph by paragraph, for a modified scene.

snippet.description:
A few words around the match; matched words sit between U+0002 and
U+0003.

userAgent.description: What the device said it was, for telling sessions apart in a list.

current.description: The session this request came from.

to.description: What it is being measured against.

atBlock.description:
Index of the first top-level block that belongs to the *new* scene.
Blocks, not characters: the cut is between paragraphs, which is how a
writer thinks about "this should have been two scenes".

baseHash.description:
The `contentHash` the split was decided against. Required, unlike on an
ordinary save: splitting rewrites prose in two places, and doing that to
a document someone else has edited would be much worse than refusing.

title.description: Title for the new scene. Defaults to the original's, with a suffix.

first.description: The original scene, now holding only the blocks before the cut.

second.description: The new scene, holding the rest.

StaleChange.description: Why a change could not be applied, for a client that has to explain it.

Standing.description:
How useful a reviewer's feedback has turned out to be.

Derived on read rather than kept in a column: it is a function of rows that
already exist, and a stored copy would only be a second thing to get wrong.

resolved.description: Notes a work's author marked resolved — them saying they acted on it.

votes.description: Net votes across everything this reviewer has written.

writePath.description: The last minute and the last fifteen.

oneOf.description: The note it came from, if it came from one and that note still stands.

body.description: Prefilled prose, if the template wants to seed the scene with a prompt.

baseHash.description:
The scene's `contentHash` when the proposal was written. `None` on rows
predating this column; those always re-anchor by their quotation.

secret.description: The key to type into an authenticator by hand.

url.description: The same key as an `otpauth://` link, for a QR code or a tap.

chapterIds.description:
Narrow them to exactly these chapters. An empty list leaves them
nowhere to write, which is not the same as everywhere.

wholeWork.description: `true` hands them the whole work again.

state.description: `open` or `resolved`; only the author of the work may resolve.

chapterId.description: Move the scene into a different chapter of the same work.

storyDate.description: Free text: fiction rarely runs on the Gregorian calendar.

targetWords.description:
A word target for this scene. Omit to leave it alone; send `null` to
clear it. The nesting is what distinguishes those two — see
`present_or_absent`.

notes.description: What this snapshot was for. Blank clears it.

penName.description:
Front matter. Each is sent only when it changes; an empty string clears
one, which is what a writer emptying the field in the UI means.

dailyWordGoal.description: The writer's daily target in words, when they have set one.

emailVerifiedAt.description:
When the address was proved. Invitations addressed to it reach this
account only once it has been.

legalName.description:
Contact details for a submission's first page. Kept on the writer rather
than the work, since they are the same for every submission.

termsVersion.description: The version of the terms they last agreed to.

totpEnabledAt.description: When two-factor sign-in was turned on.

scope.description: `work`, `chapter` or `scene` — how much of the book this froze.

page.description: Which chapter of `toc` this page holds, from zero.

toc.description:
Every chapter on offer, in order, when this is one page of them — so a
reader can move between pages and count progress along the whole book.

tags.description: Free-form labels, lowercased so `Submitted` and `submitted` are one tag.

pinned.description: Whether this is the work's pinned snapshot.

tags.description:
Tags, but not the manifest: a list of fifty snapshots has no use for
fifty manifests.

value.description: `1` upvote, `-1` downvote, `0` clears the caller's vote.

dbWritesPerSecond.description: Database calls made while serving them.

lockWaitMs.description: Sampled: how long the write lock took to get, every few seconds.

oneOf.description:
What to browse it under. Unset is allowed: plenty of writers do not
know yet.

penName.description: The name on the byline, when it is not the writer's own.

pinnedVersionId.description:
The snapshot the writer wants to find without looking — what they last
sent out.

shortTitle.description: Short form for a running header; a long title wraps and ruins it.

WorkAccess.description: What the outline tells a client about who it is to this work.

chapterIds.description:
The chapters they may change, when they were handed only some. Absent
means the whole work. Reading is never narrowed.

creator.description: Whether they started the work — the one thing an added owner is not.

subject.description: The title as it was at the time.

times.description: How many acts this line stands for.

dailyWordGoal.description: The writer's target, if they have set one.

history.description: Most recent first, one entry per day the writer showed up.

streak.description: Consecutive days up to and including today on which they wrote.

wordsToday.description: Net words on `today`, which may be negative on a day spent cutting.

info.description: A writing tool for long-form fiction, and a review surface for readers.

Password changed; every device signed out

post.summary:
Records that an entry appears in a scene. Idempotent — linking twice is what
a writer does when they are not sure whether they already did.

200.description: The change, and the scene it was applied to

delete.summary:
Soft delete: threads keep their shape, and the work's author can remove
abusive feedback from their own publication.

post.summary: Turn a reviewer's note into a line of the author's own work.

Votes surface the feedback other reviewers agree with. One vote per person
per comment; sending the same value again clears it.

A ticket to open the live channel with. A WebSocket cannot carry an
Authorization header from a browser, and a token in a URL ends up in logs,
so the socket is opened with this instead: single use, and dead in thirty
seconds whether or not it was used.

409.description: Works with co-authors would go too

get.summary: What you did, and what anyone did to a work you own. Newest first.

Everything held about the caller, as one zip they can open without us:
JSON for the records, and the manuscript files exactly as they are stored.

200.description: Every device signed in, most recent first
On; the recovery codes, shown once
A new key, not yet in force
Today, the streak, and recent history

get.summary:
Prometheus text for a dashboard to scrape. Exists only when
`SCRIPTORIUM_METRICS_TOKEN` is set, and wants it as a bearer token.
The review feed. Signed-out readers see only `public` publications.

delete.summary:
Withdrawing a publication takes its comments with it; the snapshot itself
is untouched.

get.summary:
The author gets everyone's answers; a reader gets their own back, which is
what lets the form reopen with what they already said.

post.description:
Twenty typo reports are twenty rows and one decision. Doing that one row at
a time is how a review queue stops being read at all.
post.summary: Resolve or reopen a pile of notes at once.

get.description:
A page reads only its own chapter's files, which is the point: a novel is
eighty scenes, and the first page should not wait for the last.
get.summary:
The manuscript as reviewers see it: the frozen snapshot, narrowed to the
slice the author published — whole, or a chapter at a time.

Every note on a publication, as a document. The author's only: it carries
everyone's feedback with their names on it.

200.description: Who it is now shared with

get.summary: How far everyone got — the author's view of a review in progress.

put.description:
Only ever moves the furthest mark forward: a reader who gave up in chapter
three and later skimmed the ending has still stopped in chapter three, and
that is the fact an author needs.
put.summary: Records where a reader has got to.

get.description:
Not a policy about privacy — it is about not corrupting the signal. A
reader who can see that four people found this paragraph confusing is being
told what to think about it, and the fifth mark stops meaning anything.
get.summary: A reader sees only their own marks; the author sees the totals.

200.description: The block as the viewer now sees it

get.description:
A diff answers "what did I change"; this answers the question an author
actually has in front of a pile of feedback — *which of these have I
already dealt with*. Each note is placed against the paragraph it was
anchored to, and that paragraph is followed forward into the newer text.

The author's view only. It carries everyone's notes with their names on
them, and it compares against the working draft, which is not a thing any
reader is entitled to see.

200.description: What has moved under the notes

get.summary: What has changed since reviewers saw this, note by note.

post.description:
Accepts apply from the end of the document backwards, so applying one never
shifts the positions of the ones still to come. A proposal that cannot be
placed is left pending and reported, rather than skipped silently or applied
somewhere plausible.
post.summary: Resolves every pending change in a scene at once.

put.summary:
The hot path: the editor PUTs the whole scene document. Content goes to
disk, counts and hashes go to SQLite, and an optional revision is kept so
the author can walk back through their own drafting history.

post.description:
The inverse of `split`: the absorbed scene's blocks follow this one's, in
order, and nothing is dropped at the seam.
post.summary: Folds the next scene into this one and removes it.

post.description:
The restore is itself a save: it writes a fresh revision first, so the text
being replaced stays reachable and restoring is undoable. Nothing in the
revision history is ever rewritten or removed.
post.summary: Put an earlier revision back as the working copy.

post.description:
The new scene lands immediately after the original and everything below it
shifts down, so the reading order is unchanged. Nothing is lost: every block
ends up in exactly one of the two, which is what makes `merge` its inverse.
post.summary: Cuts one scene into two at a block boundary.

get.summary: Built-ins plus anything the caller has saved as their own template.

200.description: How useful this reviewer has been

patch.description:
A label chosen in the moment ("v3") is rarely the one that helps six months
later ("before the agent's notes"), and the snapshot's text is immutable —
but what you call it should not be.
patch.summary: Renaming a snapshot after the fact.

get.summary:
The whole frozen manuscript. Authors always get their own; readers reach a
version through a publication instead.

post.summary:
Pins a snapshot as the one the writer wants to find without looking —
typically what they last sent out. Pinning another replaces it.

post.description:
Never in place, and never destructively: the working copy is snapshotted
first, automatically, so the state being replaced is one restore away. That
safety snapshot is what makes it safe to remove scenes written after the
version being restored — without it, "restore" would quietly discard them.

A scoped version restores only its own chapter or scene, leaving the rest of
the book alone.
post.summary: Puts a snapshot back as the working copy.
Tags a snapshot. Idempotent, so tagging twice is not an error.

200.description: What has happened to this work, newest first
Who else is on this work
Everyone on the work, the new one included

get.summary: Finds words in a work's working text, best matches first.

post.summary:
Freeze the current working copy. Files are copied before any row is written
so a half-copied snapshot never becomes visible.

get.description:
Each changed scene is aligned paragraph by paragraph rather than diffed as
one run of words, so a reflowed sentence does not make the rest of the scene
look edited, and a paragraph that moved says so.
get.summary: Scene-level comparison of two snapshots, or of a snapshot and the draft.
